## REQ-ACT-001

**Call and Reply use OPC UA PubSub Actions**

The call/reply pattern (Methods Call and Reply) is implemented with OPC UA PubSub Actions: a message published with Call is an ActionNetworkMessage with MessageType "ua-action-request", a message published with Reply one with MessageType "ua-action-response"; the Responder answers every ua-action-request it can decode and address with ua-action-response messages.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.1, MG 8.1.3, MG 8.2.16, MG 9.2
- Verification: schema, d7-validate, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.1-0e566ba4, MG-8.1-52bb2c17, MG-8.1.3-2f07634f, MG-8.1.3-aa30f206, MG-8.2.16-25164d36, MG-8.2.16-2cd64af0, MG-8.2.16-e118d52d, MG-9.2-15fe1339

> ua-action-request and ua-action-response must be used for the call/reply pattern over the Message Bus.
> — MG 8.1

> A Requestor must publish a ua-action-request to request the execution of one or more Actions, and the Responder must answer with a ua-action-response.
> — MG 8.1.3

> ua-action-request must be used for messages published with the method Call, ua-action-response for messages published with the method Reply.
> — MG 8.2.16

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-034 (Call/Reply) and REQ-CMP-040 (NewDataSetWriterId).

## REQ-ACT-002

**Fields of the ActionNetworkMessage**

An ActionNetworkMessage contains MessageId, MessageType, PublisherId, Timestamp (DateTime string, time of the first sending), RequestorId and Messages (JSON array of ActionRequest or ActionResponse objects). A ua-action-request additionally contains ResponseAddress and TimeoutHint (Duration in milliseconds) and may contain CorrelationData (Base64 ByteString); a ua-action-response contains neither ResponseAddress nor TimeoutHint.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.16
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.16-3f9165a4, MG-8.2.16-8f87b9eb, MG-8.2.16-9cfbdf96

> Value Range: &lt;Reply topic> Type: String Requirement: Mandatory for ua-action-request, omitted for ua-action-response
> — MG 8.2.16

> Value Range: &lt;Duration in ms> Type: Duration (Double) Requirement: Mandatory for ua-action-request, omitted for ua-action-response
> — MG 8.2.16

## REQ-ACT-003

**Action messages use the CompactEncoding and fixed content masks**

All fields of Action messages are encoded with the JSON CompactEncoding (fields with default values omitted, enumerations such as ActionState as numbers, StatusCode without Symbol). The ActionNetworkMessage contains neither DataSetClassId nor ReplyTo (JsonNetworkMessageContentMask 0x0B), the ActionRequest and ActionResponse no SequenceNumber, MessageType, PublisherId, DataSetWriterName, WriterGroupName or MinorVersion, and the RawData bit is not set (DataSetFieldContentMask 0).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.1.4, MG 8.2.16, MG 8.2.20
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.1.4-92ade777

> JsonNetworkMessageContentMask: NetworkMessageHeader, DataSetMessageHeader and PublisherId are set, all other bits are not set. This results in the value 0x0B (11).
> — MG 8.1.4

> DataSetFieldContentMask: 0. The RawData bit shall not be set for Actions.
> — MG 8.1.4

> All fields of Action messages are encoded with the JSON CompactEncoding (Part 14-7.2.5.6).
> — MG 8.1.4

Notes: The DataSetClassId of an Action is only part of its ActionMetaData (MG 8.2.19).

## REQ-ACT-004

**MessageId of Action messages**

The MessageId of an Action message is "&lt;unixTimestampInMs>-&lt;PublisherId of the sender>", i.e. the RequestorId for a ua-action-request and the PublisherId of the Responder for a ua-action-response, and is globally unique.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.16, SF-049
- Verification: schema, d7-validate, d7-monitor
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.16-8ab944d7

> Value Range: &lt;unixTimestampInMs-PublisherId of the sender> Type: String Requirement: Mandatory
> — MG 8.2.16

> A globally unique identifier for the message.
> — MG 8.2.16

> For a ua-action-request, this is the RequestorId, for a ua-action-response the PublisherId of the Responder.
> — MG 8.2.16

## REQ-ACT-005

**PublisherId is the Responder, RequestorId the Requestor**

In request and response, PublisherId is "&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>" of the Responder – the ServiceType and the decoded AppId of the Call and Reply topic – and RequestorId is "&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>" of the Requestor; both contain the AppId as unencoded Identification Link.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.16, MG 7.4
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.16-0055999c, MG-8.2.16-2a955fbc, MG-8.2.16-8e7b02eb

> The PublisherId of the Responder, in the request as well as in the response. It must correspond to the &lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId> of the Call and Reply topic, but contain the unencoded Identification Link.
> — MG 8.2.16

> The PublisherId of the Requestor, in the request as well as in the response.
> — MG 8.2.16

## REQ-ACT-006

**ResponseAddress is the Reply topic**

The ResponseAddress of a ua-action-request is the Reply topic that corresponds to the Call topic of the request ("Oi4v2/&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>/Reply/&lt;Service>[/&lt;Source>]"), and the Responder publishes its responses to this ResponseAddress.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.16, MG 9.2, MG 7.4
- Verification: schema, d7-validate, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.16-c7e6b480, MG-8.2.16-dd642483, MG-8.2.16-ec40bbe4, MG-9.2-1aace699

> The MQTT topic, the Responder shall use to publish the response.
> — MG 8.2.16

> In Open Industry 4.0 Alliance context, this must always be the Reply topic corresponding to the Call topic of the request (7.4 Method Element)
> — MG 8.2.16

> The Responder must publish the ua-action-response to the ResponseAddress given in the request, which is the corresponding Reply topic.
> — MG 9.2

Notes: Same rule from the topic side in REQ-TOP-016.

## REQ-ACT-008

**Responder stops processing after the TimeoutHint**

The Responder stops processing a request when its TimeoutHint has expired, counted from the reception of the request (the Requestor counts from the publication of the request, REQ-ACT-009).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.16, SF-051
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.16-3c2aa779, MG-8.2.16-693c2b30

> For the Responder, the TimeoutHint starts with the reception of the request; the Responder shall stop processing the request after this time.
> — MG 8.2.16

## REQ-ACT-009

**Requestor treats an expired TimeoutHint as failure**

A Requestor does not wait longer than the TimeoutHint for the final response; if none arrives within the TimeoutHint, it considers the request as failed.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.16, MG 9.2, MG 8.2.20
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.16-3d9be90a, MG-9.2-2c2c99da

> Because erroneous requests (e.g. decoding errors or unknown DataSetWriterIds) are not answered, the Requestor must not wait longer than the TimeoutHint for a response.
> — MG 8.2.16

> If the Responder does not respond within the TimeoutHint, the Requestor shall consider the request as failed (8.2.20 ActionState).
> — MG 9.2

## REQ-ACT-010

**Fields of the ActionRequest**

An ActionRequest contains DataSetWriterId and ActionTargetId (UInt16, addressing the Action of the Responder), RequestId (UInt16), ActionState 1 (Executing) and Payload (JSON object with the request fields, empty if the Action has none); it may contain MetaDataVersion and Timestamp and never contains DataSetWriterName, WriterGroupName, MinorVersion or MessageType.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.

- Verification: schema, d7-validate

> To request the execution of an Action, the value 1 (Executing) is used.

> The fields DataSetWriterName, WriterGroupName, MinorVersion and MessageType defined by OPC UA for the ActionRequest are not used in Open Industry 4.0 Alliance context and shall be omitted.
> — MG 8.2.17

## REQ-ACT-011

**RequestId is unique among pending requests**

A Requestor assigns each ActionRequest a RequestId that is unique among all its pending requests (per RequestorId); each ActionRequest of a ua-action-request has its own RequestId. Uniqueness does not depend on the CorrelationData.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.17, SF-051
- Verification: d7-monitor
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.17-0a95672e

> The Requestor shall keep the RequestId unique among all its pending requests (per RequestorId), independent of the CorrelationData.
> — MG 8.2.17

> If a ua-action-request contains several ActionRequests, each of them has its own RequestId.
> — MG 8.2.17

## REQ-ACT-012

**Fields of the ActionResponse**

An ActionResponse contains DataSetWriterId, ActionTargetId and RequestId of the related ActionRequest, Status, ActionState (1 Executing for an intermediate, 2 Done for the final response) and Payload (JSON object with the response fields; empty if the Status is Bad or the Action has none); it may contain MetaDataVersion and Timestamp and never contains DataSetWriterName, WriterGroupName, MinorVersion or MessageType.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.18, MG 8.2.20
- Verification: schema, d7-validate, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.18-1cbe23a0, MG-8.2.18-2429d9a4, MG-8.2.18-7acf7eab, MG-8.2.18-9ec81017, MG-8.2.18-ae8057a2, MG-8.2.18-c89c8bfd, MG-8.2.18-c90cc13a, MG-8.2.18-e1a40bfa, MG-8.2.18-ef569e4a

> If the Status is Bad or the Action has no response fields, the Payload is an empty object.
> — MG 8.2.18

> The fields DataSetWriterName, WriterGroupName, MinorVersion and MessageType defined by OPC UA for the ActionResponse are not used in Open Industry 4.0 Alliance context and shall be omitted.
> — MG 8.2.18

## REQ-ACT-014

**Status of the ActionResponse**

Every ActionResponse contains a Status in CompactEncoding: {} for Good, otherwise {"Code": &lt;UInt32>}, never a Symbol; a request field that breaks a constraint (e.g. wrong data type, value out of range) results in BadInvalidArgument (0x80AB0000).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.3, MG 8.2.18

- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.3-8f9384e4, MG-8.2.3-d7fec634

> The Status of an ActionResponse uses the CompactEncoding and therefore must never contain the Symbol. It must always be sent, with {} for Good (8.2.18 ActionResponse).
> — MG 8.2.3

> If at least one request field broke a constraint (e.g. wrong data type, value out of range), the Status is set to BadInvalidArgument.
> — MG 8.2.18

## REQ-ACT-015

**Sequence of an Action**

The Requestor publishes a ua-action-request with ActionState 1 to the Call topic of the Responder; the Responder publishes for every ActionRequest it can decode and address exactly one final ActionResponse with ActionState 2, the Status and the result Payload to the ResponseAddress, with the same DataSetWriterId, ActionTargetId and RequestId; the ActionResponses of one ua-action-request may be sent in one or in several ua-action-response messages. Request and response are related by RequestorId, RequestId and, if present, CorrelationData.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.20, MG 9.2, SF-051
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.20-3b95c2e3, MG-8.2.20-464e2555, MG-8.2.20-56ea1e8b, MG-8.2.20-c779a1d4, MG-9.2-4c18c5e8, MG-9.2-9997933b

> The Requestor must publish a ua-action-request with ActionState 1 (Executing) to the Call topic of the Responder (7.4 Method Element).
> — MG 8.2.20

> The Responder must publish a ua-action-response with ActionState 2 (Done), the Status and the Payload with the result to the ResponseAddress.
> — MG 8.2.20

> If a ua-action-request contains several ActionRequests, every ActionRequest that can be decoded and addressed must get exactly one final ActionResponse (ActionState 2) with the same DataSetWriterId, ActionTargetId and RequestId.
> — MG 8.2.20

> The Responder may send the ActionResponses of one ua-action-request in one or in several ua-action-response messages.
> — MG 8.2.20

> Request and response are related to each other by the RequestorId, the RequestId and the optional CorrelationData (8.2.17 ActionRequest)
> — MG 9.2

Notes: SF-051 (c), resolved C-024. The execution order of several ActionRequests is up to the Responder (MG 8.2.16).

## REQ-ACT-016

**Intermediate responses for long-running Actions**

Before the final response, the Responder may publish one or more ua-action-response messages with ActionState 1 (Executing) to the ResponseAddress to indicate the progress of a long-running Action.

- Keyword: MAY
- Levels: L1 MAY · L2 MAY · L3 MAY
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.18, MG 8.2.20
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.18-c5d9afd6, MG-8.2.20-1217e3b3

> For long-running Actions, the Responder may send intermediate responses with 1 (Executing) before the final response.
> — MG 8.2.18

Notes: A Requestor therefore accepts intermediate responses and waits for ActionState 2.

## REQ-ACT-017

**No response to undecodable, unaddressable or rejected requests**

The Responder sends no response to a request that it cannot decode or address (e.g. unknown DataSetWriterId or ActionTargetId) or that it rejects for security reasons.

- Keyword: MUST NOT
- Levels: L1 MUST NOT · L2 MUST NOT · L3 MUST NOT
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.20
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.20-0b675c28

> If a request cannot be decoded or addressed (e.g. unknown DataSetWriterId or ActionTargetId), or is rejected for security reasons, the Responder must not send a response (Part 14-6.2.11.2).
> — MG 8.2.20

Notes: "Cannot address" refers to the DataSetWriterId and ActionTargetId of the Action, not to the Source of the topic: a NewDataSetWriterId request for a Source the application neither is nor represents is answered with BadNotFound (REQ-ACT-024, SF-113).

## REQ-ACT-018

**ActionMetaData of the common services need not be published**

The ActionMetaData of the common services is defined by MG 8.4 and need not be published as ua-action-metadata; it consists of ActionTargets (ActionTargetId and Name), Request and Response (DataSetMetaDataType, Name = name of the Action, DataSetClassId of MG A2).

- Keyword: MAY
- Levels: L1 MAY · L2 MAY · L3 MAY
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: responder
- Condition: The component uses the Methods Call and Reply.
- Refs: MG 8.2.19, MG A2

> Therefore, it is not required to publish the ActionMetaData (message type ua-action-metadata) over the Message Bus.

Notes: Neither the topic of ua-action-metadata nor its fields beyond MG 8.2.19 are defined in OEC v2.0; a publication would be outside the guideline.

## REQ-ACT-019

An ActionRequest for a common service uses the DataSetWriterId reserved for its Action in MG 8.4 (NewDataSetWriterId: 8) and ActionTargetId 1; the asset the Action is executed for is addressed by the Source of the Call topic. DataSetWriterIds 4 to 7 are reserved for future common services.

## REQ-ACT-022

**NewDataSetWriterId response fields DataSetWriterId and Ttl**

The Payload of a successful NewDataSetWriterId ActionResponse contains DataSetWriterId (UInt16, a new, so far unused DataSetWriterId of the Responder, i.e. >= 10 per REQ-MSG-020) and Ttl (UInt32, seconds). This DataSetWriterId is not the DataSetWriterId of the ActionResponse itself, which is always 8.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: responder
- Condition: The component provides the common service NewDataSetWriterId.
- Refs: MG 8.4.1, MG 9.2.1
- Verification: schema, d7-validate, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.4.1-bba9d024, MG-8.4.1-c57f4602, MG-8.4.1-fbc43f91

> The service NewDataSetWriterId requests a new, so far unused, DataSetWriterId from the publisher, which executes this Action.
> — MG 8.4.1

> This response field must not be confused with the DataSetWriterId of the ActionResponse itself, which always contains the reserved DataSetWriterId 8 of the Action NewDataSetWriterId.
> — MG 8.4.1

## REQ-ACT-023

**Provided DataSetWriterId is valid for Ttl seconds**

The DataSetWriterId provided by NewDataSetWriterId can be used for the first time only within Ttl seconds after the response; the Responder keeps it reserved during this period and accepts its initial use (e.g. in a Set) only within it.

- Keyword: MUST (implicit, SF-035)
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The component requests or provides the common service NewDataSetWriterId.
- Refs: MG 8.4.1, SF-035, SF-112
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed

> Ttl contains a value, which describes the time to live of the provided DataSetWriterId in seconds. Initial usage of the provided DataSetWriterId is only possible during this period of time.
> — MG 8.4.1

> The Set that creates the DataSet carries this DataSetWriterId; for a DataSet the publisher already lists in its PublicationList, the listed DataSetWriterId is used and no new one is needed.
> — MG 8.4.1

Notes: Whether the Responder rejects a later initial use is not stated explicitly; "only possible" is read as such (implicit, SF-035). The Set that creates a DataSet carries the provided DataSetWriterId; for a DataSet already listed in the PublicationList the listed DataSetWriterId stays and the provided one lapses after Ttl. A provided DataSetWriterId that was not used within Ttl is not handed out again as long as never-used ones are left ("so far unused", REQ-ACT-022, REQ-MSG-020; SF-112).

## REQ-ACT-024

**NewDataSetWriterId for an unknown Source is answered with BadNotFound**

A Responder that neither is nor represents the Source of a NewDataSetWriterId request answers it with the final ActionResponse (ActionState 2) with the Status BadNotFound (0x803E0000) and an empty Payload.

- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
